title: Adjudicate floor-ledger micro-corners where Python/Rust/C capability tables disagree
description: From era9 codereview convergence (worker3, 2026-09-09). The three stacks cannot match each other in two corners, needing a reference-level call: (a) Refresh-path bounding: Python record() and Rust insert() do NOT bound the floor ledger on the refresh path (only on new inserts); C's fixed CONFIG_LICHEN_CAPABILITY_TABLE_CAPACITY array forces a policy, and C prunes on refresh (drop lowest-IID dead floor) — equivalent to what Python/Rust would produce if they bounded on refresh. (b) Eviction victim ordering: C floor_raise for the eviction victim happens while the victim entry is still live (matches Rust evict_lru raise-then-remove) but not Python record() popitem-then-raise; for a floorless low-IID victim the floor survives in C/Rust where Python drops it. Also note C purge_expired now captures no floors at all, matching Python purge_expired (Rust has no expiry path). Current C semantics: lichen/subsys/lichen/gateway/capability_announce.c floor_prune/floor_raise with pending-raisers-as-candidates, landed in era9. Decide whether these micro-corner divergences need reference-stack amendments (and shared corpus vectors pinning them) or documented tolerance.
